_source: coral-xyz/sealevel-attacks @ 24555d0 (no licence; labels only, no code copied) — https://github.com/coral-xyz/sealevel-attacks/tree/master/programs
_method: Recall: report the class on every vulnerable variant. Precision: nothing on safe variants except declared crossClass entries, which must keep appearing (printed with their reason every run).

secure.owner-check: 1/secure equals 2-owner-checks/insecure modulo one import, the module name and a log typo; it never checks the token account's program owner

4-initialization.note: the 'secure' variant errors when the flag is unset — it blocks the first init and permits re-init (inverted polarity, KV-014), so it is labelled vulnerable

5-arbitrary-cpi.note: insecure builds the instruction with spl_token::instruction::transfer, whose check_program_account gate returns IncorrectProgramId for any id other than spl_token::ID (verified in spl-token 3.5.0; the fixture's Cargo.lock resolves spl-token 3.2.0, so confirm the gate there before relying on this label) — FP-7; score it as hygiene, not arbitrary CPI

8-pda-sharing.note: the fixture's transfer authority is the `authority` Signer, not the pool PDA; illustrative

9-closing-accounts.note: sentinel-era Anchor semantics (these programs pin anchor-lang 0.20.1)

_not_covered: rounding (both directions) and precision loss have no fixture — write our own
